About
 
Move beyond the page and into real life.
 
 The technologies, people, and ideas transforming our world—for one day in Wynwood, Miami. 
 
 Don’t just read about what’s next. Step inside. Interact. Test. Play. Question. Repeat. 
 
 The future is here. Now experience it for yourself. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Questions we’re asking.
 
And the people answering them.

       What’s the secret to more good years?  A Good Time, for a Long Time Dan Buettner, Founder, Blue Zones + Dr. Eric Verdin, President and CEO, The Buck Institute for Research on Aging + Katie Drummond, Global Editorial Director, WIRED

       What if The Onion launched an alt-right podcast?  Satire, and who it’s for now Ben Collins, CEO, The Onion 
          
     
    Ben Collins is the CEO of The Onion and a journalist covering online disinformation and extremism. Between 2018 and 2024 he worked at NBC News, where he covered how movements such as QAnon influence politics and media.
     
    In 2024 he helped assemble the group that acquired The Onion, leading efforts to rebuild and expand the satirical publication. In 2026 The Onion acquired the conspiracy theory platform Infowars.
     
    Photo: The Boston Globe/Getty Images
     
     
     
      
     
    •  
  •  
      
       Who owns the future of AI?  A lawsuit gives us some clues Clément Delangue, Cofounder and CEO, Hugging Face 
          
     
    Clément Delangue is the CEO and a cofounder of Hugging Face, an open and collaborative platform for AI builders. Hugging Face hosts more than 3 million models and over 1 million datasets and spaces, with the goal of democratizing AI by distributing it to a broad base of users and developers.
     
    Photo: James Jackman
     
     
     
      
     
    •  
  •  
      
       What if you pointed a camera at Elon Musk and didn’t look away?  Musk film screening and Q&A Alex Gibney, Film Director + Ashley St. Clair, Writer and Policy Advocate 
          
     
    Alex Gibney is an Oscar-, Emmy-, Grammy-, Peabody-, and WGA Award-winning filmmaker celebrated for his incisive and gripping documentaries. His landmark works include Taxi to the Dark Side, Going Clear, Enron, The Inventor, and In Restless Dreams.
     
    Gibney is currently producing and directing a Hulu documentary about Luigi Mangione. His latest films, Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie, inspired by Salman Rushdie’s memoir, and Musk, an unvarnished examination of Elon Musk, are set for theatrical release in fall 2026.
     
    Ashley St. Clair is a mother, writer, media personality, and policy advocate whose work focuses on First Amendment protections, law, technology, culture, and government accountability. Her perspective is informed by nearly a decade spent inside conservative politics as a political strategist and media operative within the Trump and MAGA movement. A graduate of the University of Colorado with a degree in philosophy, she is currently pursuing her Juris Doctor.
     
    St. Clair is a frequent presence across national and international media and policy forums, with a focus on disinformation and stronger legal protections for women and children in the digital age.
     
    Photo of Alex Gibney: Andrew Brucker
     
     
     
       
     
    •  
  •  
      
       What if you could talk to a dolphin?  Spoiler: You can. Here’s how Dr. Denise Herzing, Founder and Research Director, Wild Dolphin Project 
          
     
    Dr. Denise Herzing is the founder and research director of the Wild Dolphin Project, coeditor of Dolphin Communication and Cognition, and an affiliate assistant professor in biological sciences at Florida Atlantic University in Boca Raton. She has studied Atlantic spotted dolphins every summer since 1985.
     
    Dr. Herzing is a 2004 fellow with the Explorers Club, a 2008 Guggenheim fellow, and a 2021 member of the Women Divers Hall of Fame. Recently, she was awarded Conservationist of the Year for 2027 by Wild About Wildlife and was included in Time magazine’s list of the 100 most influential people in AI. She is a founding member of the Marine Mammal Society, a scientific adviser for the American Cetacean Society and the Whale Sanctuary, and is on the board of Schoolyard Films.
     
     
     
      
     
    •  
  •  
      
       What if we could bring back the woolly mammoth?  De-extinction, and what comes after Ben Lamm, Cofounder and CEO, Colossal Biosciences 
          
     
    Ben Lamm is a cofounder and the CEO of Colossal Biosciences, the world’s first de-extinction company. A serial technology entrepreneur, he has spent more than 20 years building companies at the intersection of artificial intelligence, emerging technology, conservation, and space innovation.
     
    Prior to Colossal, he founded and led Hypergiant, Conversable, Chaotic Moon, and Team Chaos, all of which were successfully acquired. Lamm serves on the board of directors of the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation and is a fellow and trustee of the Explorers Club.
     
    Photo: Colossal Biosciences
     
     
     
      
     
    •  
  •  
      
       What if you could put a social network in front of a jury?  Suing the platforms Mark Lanier, Trial Lawyer 
          
     
    Mark Lanier is a top trial lawyer who has won some of the largest verdicts in US history, representing people harmed by the world’s most powerful companies. Most recently, he won the nation’s first social-media addiction trial, a landmark verdict against Meta and Google’s YouTube.
     
    An inductee in the National Trial Lawyer Hall of Fame, Lanier also teaches the craft of trial advocacy to more than a thousand lawyers each summer at his Lanier Trial Academy. He has authored several books on faith and law, and leads a 750-member Bible class in Houston, where he lives with his wife, Becky, and their family.
     
     
     
      
     
    •  
  •  
      
       Where should the VC dollars go next?  Investing in the ideas, people, and movements shaping the future Alexis Ohanian, Founder, Seven Seven Six and Cofounder, Reddit 
          
     
    Alexis Ohanian is a tech founder and venture capitalist. He is the cofounder and former executive chair of Reddit, which he started in 2005, left in 2010, and then returned to lead in 2014 before resigning in protest in 2020. In 2020, Ohanian founded Seven Seven Six, a venture capital firm with over $1.3 billion in assets under management.
     
    He is the founding control owner of Angel City Football Club and Los Angeles Golf Club, and the founder of ATHLOS. Ohanian is also an investor in Chelsea FC Women. In 2022, he launched the 776 Foundation to support marginalized individuals and announced a $20 million commitment to climate action through his 776 Fellowship Program. He’s also the bestselling author of Without Their Permission and creator of the Business Dad podcast, exploring what it means to be a dad in today’s world.
     
     
     
      
     
    •  
  •  
      
       What if the next election is won by creators, not campaigns?  After the midterms CJ Pearson, Political Influencer and Republican Strategist + Kat Abughazaleh, Researcher, Journalist, and Former Congressional Candidate 
          
     
    CJ Pearson is a nationally recognized conservative commentator and political strategist, and the chair of the Next250 political action committee. As the national co-chair of the Republican National Committee Youth Advisory Council, he played a pivotal role in mobilizing young conservatives during the 2024 election, helping connect the RNC and the influencer community. In 2025, Pearson was recognized by Time as one of the 100 most-influential people on the internet. Beyond his public profile, Pearson is the founder and CEO of the Pearson Company, a creator-led political influencer agency, and a regular contributor to Fox News.
     
    Kat Abughazaleh is a Palestinian-American researcher, journalist, and former congressional candidate. Abughazaleh’s organization KAPOW, formed after her close election loss, works to integrate mutual aid and direct action into electoral politics by using campaign resources to help people rather than manipulate them. Her writing has appeared in Mother Jones and The New Republic. Abughazaleh lives in Chicago with her partner, Ben, and their two cats, Heater and Dragon. She hates ICE, Flock, and genocide, but finds joy in her loving family, mediocre knitting, and reading space operas.
     
    Photo of CJ Pearson: Alan Shindleman. Photo of Kat Abughazaleh: Eliana Melmed
     
     
     
       
     
    •  
  •  
      
       What happens when you push AI to the limit?  Hilarity ensues Evan Ratliff, Writer and Host, Shell Game + Husk, Comedian and Face of AI Satire Online 
          
     
    Evan Ratliff has been contributing feature stories to WIRED for over 25 years. He’s also the writer and host of the podcast Shell Game, and the author of The Mastermind: A True Story of Murder, Empire, and a New Kind of Crime Lord.
     
    Husk is a comedian known for his satirical takes on AI. His deadpan exchanges with ChatGPT’s voice model have received over 800 million views and earned Husk 1 million followers, including Justin Bieber, Jack Black, Nikki Glaser, Tim Robinson, and Bob Odenkirk. Coverage of his work has appeared in Vanity Fair, WIRED, Vice, and Fast Company, which dubbed him “Sam Altman’s worst nightmare.” He has an original series in development with The Onion and has done brand partnerships with CeraVe, Ninja, and ON.
     
    Photo of Evan Ratliff: Jonah Green. Photo of Husk: Husk

       What will 2099 be like?  And will humans still be in charge? Hunter Schafer, Actress and Artist + Silka Luisa, Showrunner, Creator, and Executive Producer 
          
     
    Hunter Schafer is an actress and artist best known for her pivotal role in HBO’s drama series Euphoria. She also recently appeared in Mother Mary, The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, Cuckoo, and Kinds of Kindness. She will appear in the forthcoming Blade Runner 2099 miniseries as well as in Tom Ford’s adaptation of the Anne Rice novel Cry to Heaven. Schafer is also an artist trained in illustration and painting.
     
    Silka Luisa is the showrunner, creator, and executive producer of Prime Video’s forthcoming limited series Blade Runner 2099. Previously, she served as showrunner and executive producer of Apple TV+’s Shining Girls, and wrote and executive produced the pilot The Wilding for USA Network. She also wrote on Netflix’s Fear Street film trilogy and served as supervising producer on the first season of Paramount TV+’s Halo series. She was a consulting producer on Strange Angel, created by Mark Heyman.
     
    Photo of Hunter Schafer: Neilson Barnard. Photo of Silka Luisa: Jonny Marlow

Experiences
 
Work you can walk into.
 
 
 
 
 
Refuel. Regroup. Recharge.
 
Step into three spaces shaped by Nas and other leading entrepreneurs who embody the spirit of Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business, each offering a look at what fuels their ideas, businesses, and momentum.
 
REFUEL with ceremonial-grade matcha from Rocky’s Matcha. REGROUP in a lounge curated by Nas, featuring brands, tools, and essentials that fuel his entrepreneurial world. RECHARGE with a presence from Cymbiotika alongside emerging approaches to wellness, meditation, longevity, and digital wellbeing.
 
Just like Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business is the card that gives back all you put in, these spaces help guests taste, try, and discover the products, rituals, and perspectives that help today’s entrepreneurs stay fueled, find inspiration, and reset for what’s next.
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
Kinda Studios
 
Emergence
 
Emergence is an evidence-based immersive sensory experience designed to expand liminal states of consciousness, spark creative insight, and deepen senses of presence. Guests are guided through distinct phases designed to open the mind and body, and unlock neural states connected to mindfulness, transformation, and creativity. Using cutting-edge neuroaesthetic science, the experience encompasses a meditative journey through visual, sonic, and vibroacoustic immersion to move the mind into a state rich with ideation, where ideas, creativity, and insight can emerge. Grounded in evidence-based neuroscience, the experience uses carefully crafted sensory design to support states of expansion.
 
 Read moreRead less 
About Kinda Studios
 
Kinda is a neuroscience studio and lab maximising the impact of art, culture, and technology through science. By translating academic insight into creative experiences, they make science tangible as something to see, feel, and remember.
 
Cofounded by Robyn Landau, a neuroaesthetics researcher, designer, and cultural entrepreneur, and Katherine Templar Lewis, an interdisciplinary scientist and expert in neuroscience, neuroaesthetics, cognition, and behavioral psychology, Kinda unites disciplines to pioneer new approaches to creativity, human experience, and social impact.
 
From Your Inner Symphony at London’s Barbican Center, which transformed live biometric responses into visuals and collective sounds, to real-time neurotechnologies visualising the neural emotional states, immersive experiences with 113 Spring, and original projects with ITV, Audible, On, and SXSW, Kinda turns cutting-edge brain science into sensory and embodied experiences to support states of connection.
 
Emergence, Kinda Studios. Photo: Kunning Huang/CKA
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
Marina Abramović
 
Slow Walking, 2026, Avatar Performance powered by TAEX
 
Slow Walking by Marina Abramović, powered by TAEX, is a first-of-its-kind avatar performance by a lifelike digital twin of a major living performance artist. The installation and limited-edition digital artwork offer a rare opportunity to encounter Abramović’s Slow Walk Method as intended by the artist herself. This mindfulness exercise designed to heighten awareness to the present and strengthen endurance. Guests are invited into a meditative durational encounter with radically decelerated time, heightened perception, and the transformative potential of digital performance.
 
The project premiered as part of the landmark exhibition “Transforming Energy” at the Gallerie dell’Accademia di Venezia during the 61st Venice Biennale. For Abramović, technology introduces new opportunities to explore the question of presence, and with this piece she continues to pioneer new frontiers of art.
 
 Read moreRead less 
About Marina Abramović
 
Marina Abramović is a performance artist renowned for pioneering performance art, pushing its representation from an alternative medium into fine contemporary art. Known as the “godmother of performance art,” she has used her own body as both the subject and medium of her work for over 50 years, testing her physical and mental limits to explore the relationship between the performer and the audience.
 
Instead of keeping distance, Abramović demands active participation. Her endurance art pushes past exhaustion, pain, and danger. Her involvement is more than bodily and conceptual; it is existential. And her legacy is undeniably genius.
 
 
 
 
 
    
 
 
NASA XOSS
 
Experience the same training environment as NASA’s Artemis astronauts and transport yourself to the Moon, where you can explore the lunar surface and take part in immersive mission scenarios using high fidelity digital twins of the spacecraft, rovers, habitats, and interconnected subsystems that will support future lunar missions. Guests in this hyperrealistic activation are immersed in the environment, conditions, and mission scenarios of an astronaut crew living on Mars and the moon, experiencing space and the world beyond our planet with XR simulation, training scenarios, and education.
 
 Read moreRead less 
About NASA XOSS
 
Developed in partnership with NASA’s Advanced Operations Concepts Lab, XR Operations Support System, or XOSS, is a multiuser XR simulation software developed by Buendea to help prepare for the next generation of human space exploration using hyperrealistic environments.
 
Buendea was founded by Julian Reyes Copello, a software developer and thought leader in the XR and AI industry. Copello also led technology strategy at the eco-innovation group Parley for the Oceans, with a focus on generating impact and solutions to protect our oceans. He was the director of technology for Miami’s III Points Festival from 2016 to 2018.
 
His work has been featured at SXSW, Nvidia GTC, US Capitol, Tribeca Film Festival, Geneva Film Festival, and Aspen Ideas Festival. Previously, Julian served as director of Fusion Media Group Labs, a team dedicated to immersive and innovative content creation under the Univision company umbrella, and as a producer for Art House Records, an award-winning recording studio in Miami, Florida.
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
Refik Anadol
 
Refik Anadol’s Large Nature Model is the world’s first open-access generative AI model dedicated to nature, incorporating ongoing research into collective visual representations of the natural world.
 
Since 2016, Anadol has utilized machine intelligence as a collaborator of human imagination, pioneering custom models to process vast archives and datasets to unfold unrecognized layers in our external realities.
 
Anadol’s installation encourages us to rethink our engagement with the physical world, public art, decentralized networks, and the creative potential of AI.
 
 Read moreRead less 
About Refik Anadol
 
Refik Anadol is an internationally renowned media artist and pioneer in the aesthetics of data and machine intelligence. He is the director and cofounder of Refik Anadol Studio in Los Angeles and a lecturer at UCLA’s Department of Design Media Arts.
 
Anadol minted the first fully immersive digital artwork NFT in September 2021 and coined the terms “AI data painting” and “AI data sculpture” to encapsulate his groundbreaking exploration into the creative capacities of artificial intelligence. His work locates creativity at the intersection of humans and machines, offering us radical visualizations of our digitized memories and expanding the possibilities of interdisciplinary arts.
 
Anadol is also the cofounder of Dataland, the world’s first museum of AI arts, at The Grand LA in Downtown Los Angeles. Opened in June 2026, Dataland delivers unparalleled, omni-sensory experiences at a scale and quality never before realized, with real-time interactions between art, architecture, and audience.
 
 
 
 
 
    
 
 
Unitree Robotics
 
Meet the future of humanoid robotics. Get hands-on with Unitree Robotics’ G1 humanoid robot, a compact, remarkably agile glimpse into the next generation of human-machine interaction.
 
Watch it move, react, and perform in real time, and experience the technology shaping tomorrow’s world. This is a can’t-miss activation as the robot greets guests and roams the festival grounds, associating with curious festivalgoers and forward-thinking brands.
 
 
 
 
    
 
 
Lumenate
 
Your inner world awaits
 
Step away for a moment, close your eyes and discover vivid inner worlds. Immerse yourself in a kaleidoscope of colors created by your own mind. Feel completely present, effortlessly brought to a state of mental stillness. Experience Nova by Lumenate: flickering light with powerful sound, and a glimpse into the future of wellness technology.
 
 
 
 
    
 
 
Somadome
 
Found in hundreds of locations, from top resort spas to performance facilities, clinics, and private homes, Somadome is the world’s first immersive wellness dome. In just 20 minutes, a self-guided session of light, color, and binaural sound shifts a guest’s state, with no practice or expertise required.
 
 
 
 
    
 
 
NuraLogix
 
Anura Magic Mirror
 
The Anura Magic Mirror turns an everyday action into a snapshot of personal wellness. Users simply sit in front of the tabletop mirror and take a 30-second selfie — no wearables, sensors or physical contact required.
 
Using NuraLogix’s AI-powered Transdermal Optical Imaging™ technology, the mirror analyzes subtle changes in facial blood flow and, within seconds, translates them into a range of health and wellness insights on heart and breathing rate, physiological age, cardiovascular and metabolic health, stress, and more.
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
Reka
 
Reka builds the infrastructure that runs and trains AI systems to understand and simulate the physical world in real time — the kind of technology being developed to help robots and machines act in the real world.
 
At WIRED World Fair, you can direct a live generative experience: describe what happens and watch it unfold instantly.

    Questions
     
    Before you come.
     
     
     Who attends WIRED World Fair? 
     
    This event is for innovators, creators, investors, early adopters, technologists, and enthusiasts — anyone who wants a glimpse into the cutting edge from across industries and to connect with like-minded peers from diverse backgrounds.
     
     
     
     Where is WIRED World Fair located? 
     
    The event will take place at The Sacred Space in Miami's Wynwood neighborhood, located at 105 NE 24th St., Miami, FL.
     
     
     
     How do I get to the event? Is there parking? 
     
    There is limited street parking in the neighborhood. Valet is available onsite. We highly suggest using ride-share services, or plan to valet your vehicle.
     
     
     
     Is The Sacred Space handicap accessible? 
     
    Yes, the venue is 100% ADA accessible. Should you have any specific questions or needs, please contact us at tickets@wired.com.
     
     
     
     What is your cancellation policy? 
     
    Tickets are nonrefundable. If you have purchased a ticket and are unable to attend, you may transfer your ticket to a colleague or friend. Please email us at tickets@wired.com with the name and email address of the person you are transferring your registration to by November 1 and we will do our best to accommodate.
     
     
     
     Can I transfer my ticket? 
     
    Please email tickets@wired.com to request a transfer.
     
     
     
     Is there an age restriction? 
     
    Guests must be 18+ to attend.
     
     
     
     Who do I contact if I have additional questions? 
     
    For sponsorship inquiries, email jane_buhks@condenast.com.
     
    For press and media requests, email cydney_gasthalter@condenast.com.
     
    For general event and registration inquiries, email tickets@wired.com.
